guidelines: Never rewrite superseded archived evidence; recover through one documented adjacent pair.
A failed quality run must retain the exact failing gate output instead of only a heartbeat or wrapper error.
Increase coverage through behaviorally relevant tests; do not lower thresholds, omit files, or add blanket exclusions.
Keep this corrective limited to reliable redelivery and diagnosis; general performance optimization remains a successor Work Item.

intent.problem: The documentationAlignment implementation passed local full quality twice but PR #415 failed twice at the end of hosted project-test. The generated-alignment regression depended on the predecessor active Contract existing, so it passed before Finish and failed after archival in a clean checkout. run_quality_gate.py also cached the detailed output into a runner-local file while smoke.yml published only a timing table, preventing direct diagnosis from Actions. The implementation sat at only 85.03 percent local coverage, so focused branch coverage also needed a stable margin.
constraints: Preserve predecessor archive evidence and closed PR #415 exactly.
Use the repository's adjacent recovery-pair exception; do not bypass the one-Work-Item PR rule.
Do not weaken project-test, coverage, CI evidence, or hosted required-job semantics.
Do not absorb general performance architecture or release work.
Obtain clean Linux evidence before claiming the root cause.
intent.rationale: A fresh recovery Work Item can add missing diagnostic retention and meaningful branch coverage while keeping the predecessor audit record immutable. Linux reproduction plus repeated hosted verification distinguishes a real fix from another blind rerun.
